scope: Resolve the pass-153 lead asking when and why '노동운동' disappeared from Private School Act Article 58(1)(4).

findings.claim: Law No.7802, promulgated 2005-12-29 and effective 2006-07-01, removed '노동운동' from Private School Act Article 58(1)(4).
findings.before: 정치운동 또는 노동운동을 하거나 집단적으로 수업을 거부하거나 또는 어느 정당을 지지 또는 반대하기 위하여 학생을 지도ㆍ선동한 때
findings.after: 정치운동을 하거나 집단적으로 수업을 거부하거나 또는 어느 정당을 지지 또는 반대하기 위하여 학생을 지도ㆍ선동한 때

findings.claim: MOLEG's official amendment rationale expressly says the reform excluded labor movement from private-school teacher dismissal grounds.
findings.note: The official reason groups this change with reforms intended to improve democratic operation, transparency and public character of private schools. This proves the stated amendment rationale, not the subjective motive of every legislator.

findings.claim: The deletion was not part of the 1999 teacher-union legalization amendment itself: the 1999 Constitutional Court decision still adjudicated the 1981-version labor-movement clause, while the statutory deletion occurred in Law No.7802 in 2005 and took effect in 2006.
findings.caution: This timing does not by itself prove that teacher-union legalization caused the 2005 deletion. Bill committee records are still needed for causal linkage.

findings.claim: By the 2008/2011 statutory text Article 58(1)(4) no longer contained 노동운동, while Article 59 expressly recognized leave for a teacher serving as a full-time union official under the Teacher Union Act.

event_updates.action: deleted 노동운동 from Article 58(1)(4) dismissal ground

event_updates.note: labor-movement wording survived into the late twentieth century and was removed by Law No.7802
chronologically precedes deletion; committee/drafting records required before asserting coordination

adversarial_checks: Do not say the labor-movement clause disappeared in 1999; official amendment history places deletion in Law No.7802 (2005).
Do not equate promulgation date 2005-12-29 with effective date; the relevant provisions took effect 2006-07-01.
Do not infer that Teacher Union Act legalization caused the deletion solely from chronology.
Do not treat the 1999 Constitutional Court decision as approving post-2006 text; it reviewed the 1981-version clause.
Do not erase the separate Article 55 service-rule incorporation path when Article 58 changed.
Do not infer that removal of a dismissal ground legalized all teacher collective action.
Do not infer individual legislator motive from the official general amendment rationale.
Do not back-project post-2006 Article 58 wording into Rhee-era or 1989 enforcement.
Keep Article 59 union-official leave as a separate legal mechanism from Article 58 dismissal grounds.
Preserve the still-open question of the exact committee amendment/deliberation path that inserted this deletion into the 2005 omnibus private-school reform.
